developments: Ranked for this audience. (1) Consumer personal agents that work in the background and reach out proactively went mainstream-adjacent. Meta's Muse is the one people outside tech ask about (Vergecast), Mollick and Muse's designer describe proactive outreach, and Big Technology documents concrete failures such as wrong doctor numbers and bank balances leaked to a work Slack. (2) Assistants grounded in personal context arrived on Apple devices: the Siri AI beta and the HomeView display with face-based user switching. Independent hands-on tests show real gains in retrieving personal data, alongside silent source gaps, failed hand-offs and a skeptical device verdict. (3) AI moved into the OS. Googlebooks shipped with Magic Pointer, semantic file search and Rambler dictation. Microsoft made MXC agent containment generally available but pushed Copilot's local context and actions to 'coming months', and the Gemini app added a tasks mode plus 40+ app connectors for paying users. (4) Computer-use agents keep improving in practitioner tests (Mollick's Blender, Vo's billing ticket, Holo4). The evidence still favours tool/API lanes over GUI clicking, and some sites are now blocking agents outright (JPMorgan, Amazon vs Muse). (5) Research cautions: heavy delegation produced invalid work nobody caught, prompting fails without domain vocabulary, the GUI is not a fallback, and voice AI shifts opinions while sycophancy shapes only how users feel. The personal-context setups of power users are brittle and costly to maintain.
missing_perspectives: No accessibility users, even though voice dictation, face recognition and agents matter most to them. No non-technical everyday users reporting their own experience beyond anecdotes (Cornell's mother, people asking the Vergecast hosts). No privacy advocates or security researchers independently assessing Muse, Grokbot or HomeView's camera-based recognition and Gmail/Instagram access; the privacy points come from hosts and vendors. No non-US or non-English users (the Siri AI beta is English-only, Game Finder is US-only). No independent long-term reviews of Muse itself, of Gemini tasks or of Windows Copilot actions. No OpenAI-side consumer product evidence beyond Mollick's mentions of dots. No research on wearables or glasses this window.
balance: Accepted items: 21 from 14 publishers. Vendor: Google x2, Microsoft, and Meta via the Muse designer. Independent journalism and reviews: Vergecast x2, MKBHD x2. Practitioner: NN/g x2, Claire Vo x2, Sam Witteveen x2. Commentary: Mollick x2, Big Technology. Research: arXiv x3. Formats are mixed: written (Google, Microsoft, NN/g, Mollick, arXiv), video (MKBHD, Witteveen) and podcast (Verge, Big Technology, Claire Vo). Piece 01 draws on Google, Microsoft, Mollick, Claire Vo, The Verge, MKBHD and NN/g. Piece 02 draws on arXiv, Mollick, Google, NN/g, Big Technology, Claire Vo, The Verge, Witteveen and MKBHD. Piece 03 draws on arXiv, Mollick, Microsoft, NN/g, Big Technology, Claire Vo, The Verge and Witteveen. Vendor claims are paired with independent checks: Google Argon safety against the arXiv delegation study, Holo4 and Vo's tests; Google's Googlebook claims against MKBHD; Microsoft against Witteveen; Apple against NN/g and MKBHD. The set leans toward US tech-insider voices and agent and device news. Voice evidence is thin, with one lab study plus HomeView and Siri impressions. Duplicates of the Argon launch, MXC and HomeView were deferred in favour of the more direct items.
